ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-clearance screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs, attorneys-in-fact, and commercial counterparties against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List (including Egypt-related designations), EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists, the Egyptian domestic terrorist-designation list issued by the Egyptian Cabinet and the Ministry of Justice, and Interpol Red Notices; Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) for foreign and domestic Politically Exposed Persons, their family members, and close associates pursuant to Article 4 of Law No. 80 of 2002 as amended by Law No. 154 of 2019, FATF Recommendations 12 and 13, and EMLCU Customer Due Diligence guidance; for the ISIC 4669 dry-bulk sulfur mineral ore trade, the banking AML risk tier is Low_Risk_Standard and the designated payment rails are SWIFT LC and Standby Letter of Credit, requiring documentary compliance screening at both GAFI incorporation stage and bank account opening stage. Transaction monitoring and suspicious transaction reporting (STR) obligations pursuant to Articles 14-15 of the AML Law are triggered at the banking and trading execution phase.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) Investor Services One-Stop Shop and e-Services Platform (www.gafi.gov.eg), operating under Law No. 72 of 2017; the approved name is subsequently keyed into the Commercial Registry maintained under Law No. 34 of 1976 by the Ministry of Trade and Industry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official statutory company name of an Egyptian LLC must be rendered in Arabic script. A Latin-alphabet transliteration may be filed additionally for banking, trademark, and international trade purposes, but the Arabic name governs all legal identity matters, registration acts, and litigation. The name must not merely describe a generic sector activity, must avoid exact or phonetically near-identical similarity to existing registered names and trademarks, must be consistent with the object clause, and must not mislead as to the company's nature, nationality, or public status. GAFI applies a strict exact-match and near-identical phonetic similarity test against existing companies, brands, and protected commercial names.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Foreign country names and demonyms of third-party states
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon receipt of a GAFI name-rejection notice, the applicant, through Egyptian counsel, may file a written administrative grievance with the GAFI Legal Affairs and Complaints Department within 15 working days of the rejection date; GAFI must issue a reasoned decision on the grievance within 30 days. If the grievance is denied or deemed denied, the applicant may initiate an administrative appeal before the Cairo Administrative Court (Egyptian Council of State) within 60 days of the adverse decision pursuant to the State Council Law (Law No. 106 of 2013). A rejected applicant may concurrently re-file a modified name that cures the stated objection. Name reservation, once granted, is valid for 30 days and may be extended once for an additional 30 days upon payment of the applicable GAFI fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole statutory registered office. GAFI and the Commercial Registry require a physical Egyptian office lease evidenced by a notarized lease contract (title deed or registered sublease), which must be filed at incorporation and maintained for the life of the LLC. A virtual office may be used only as an auxiliary correspondence address and cannot satisfy the legal requirement for service of process, statutory books, or commercial substance for an LLC engaged in ISIC 4669 dry-bulk sulfur trading. For the sulfur mineral ore trading activity, the office must demonstrate adequate administrative substance, including premises, personnel capacity, and records location; the Suez Canal Economic Zone (if utilized) applies its own office-leasing rules consistent with this requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 20-35% probability of an unannounced or short-notice physical on-site verification by GAFI, the Commercial Registry, or the Egyptian Tax Authority within the first 12 months post-incorporation for a standard LLC in the industrial mineral trading sector. Tax authority attendance checks, VAT desk audits, and AML-supervisory visits increase overall inspection exposure, while routine unannounced inspections are more likely for licensed or free-zone entities than for a standard non-licensed commercial LLC.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 159 of 1981 (Egyptian Companies Law, as amended); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, Arts. 25-27; Executive Regulations, Trademark and Commercial Registration Rules; applicable formation sections: Law 159/1981 Arts. 6-12 (unified LLC incorporation contract and registration).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Companies Registration and Commercial Registry Department, Cairo One-Stop Shop.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association (Incorporation Contract) with certified Arabic-language version.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: LLC minimum subscribed capital: EGP 50,000 divided into equal shares of EGP 100 or more; no statutory escrow account mandate, but bank certificate of deposit of paid-up capital is mandatory before registration; non-cash contributions must be fully covered by an independent valuation certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Incorporation Contract of the Company, registered under the Commercial Registry of the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), is hereby ratified and the statutory seat at [Registered Address], Cairo, Egypt, is adopted as the Company's official address for service of process. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the subscription of the issued share capital is acknowledged as fully subscribed per the capital schedule annexed to the Incorporation Contract and that the minimum paid-up capital requirement is duly satisfied. RESOLVED FINALLY, that [name] is appointed General Manager and [name] is appointed Compliance and Licensing Officer, with joint authority to open bank accounts, execute lease and insurance deeds, and file all statutory declarations before GAFI, the Egyptian Tax Authority, and the Environmental and Civil Defense authorities, effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Name Reservation and Initial GAFI Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop / Commercial Registry Name Reservation Department, Cairo
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit name reservation request through GAFI online portal or counter; verify name uniqueness and compliance with Arabic naming rules; obtain official name reservation certificate valid for 60 days. Prepare preliminary memorandum of association for pre-approval.
required_dossiers: Notarized power of attorney from all founding shareholders
Valid passport copies of all shareholders and managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name is rejected due to similarity, resubmit with a revised corporate name citation; if documentation is deficient, cure within 15 days via GAFI objection window and re-file corrected dossiers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Certification of Capital and Capital Deposit Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt; escrow/account opening unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional corporate account in the Company's name, deposit the minimum paid-up capital (EGP 50,000 or higher per contract), and obtain an official capital deposit certificate stating the account holder, deposit date, and amount in EGP.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of shareholders and signatories
Target capital schedule with share allocation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bank queries ultimate beneficial ownership, supply signed declaration of direct ownership and source-of-funds statement; the deposit certificate may be re-issued with corrected language to satisfy GAFI.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Incorporation Contract and Share Subscription Signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Notary and Documentation Office / Regional Asyut or Cairo Notary Public (Maktab Al-Shahr Al-Aqari)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the authorized notary to authenticate the signatures of all founding shareholders on the Arabic-language Incorporation Contract; verify share subscription schedules and approval of articles; pay share of notary and stamp duty fees (estimated USD 30, included in total).
required_dossiers: Certified Arabic Incorporation Contract with appendices
Power of attorney if shareholder signs by proxy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notary raises substantive conflict with Law 159/1981, amend articles by executing an addendum and re-notarize; in case of missing corporate approval, obtain unanimous written consent resolution of shareholders and re-submit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Commercial Registry Registration and Issuance of Incorporation Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Registration Department (One-Stop Shop, Cairo)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Incorporation Contract with GAFI; pay the state registration fee (approx. USD 120); verify corporate purpose under ISIC 4669 allowing wholesale trading of sulfur and mineral ores; obtain Commercial Registration Certificate (Waraqit Qaid) and GAFI incorporation certificate.
required_dossiers: Lease contract or ownership title for registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a deviation letter for scope or capital deficiencies, submit a statement of correction within 30 days; if registration lapses, re-file after curing objection; appeal before GAFI's Legal Affairs Committee within 15 days of adverse decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Issuance of Consolidated Tax Card
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — Taxpayer Registration Office (Cairo Central Branch)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete ETA tax card application form (Form 101), declare corporate income tax, VAT, and payroll regimes; submit incorporation certificate and registered lease; ETA issues consolidated Tax Card including VAT certificate and corporate income tax file number.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation and commercial registration certificates
Certified lease agreement and utility invoice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ETA requires additional supporting record for real estate address, provide notarized lease and an official electricity meter record; if tax card delayed beyond SLA, escalate to ETA Inspection and Registration Department.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Chamber of Commerce Enrollment, National Publication, and Operational Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federation of Egyptian Chambers of Commerce (Cairo Lubrication Office) and GAFI Publication Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Enroll the company in the general commercial register at the competent Chamber of Commerce; effect publication summary in the official commercial newspaper (Gazette); activate operational bank account using the full incorporation and tax card portfolio.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If chamber enrollment is rejected for unverified membership, re-submit with attested translation of certificate; if publication is delayed, obtain an excerpt of the Gazette filing from GAFI's publication bureau and include it in the annual audit file.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) — Licensing and Approval Portfolio; Ministry of Trade and Industry (General Organization for Export and Import Control, GOEIC) for sulfur import-export registration.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Governorate-Issued Commercial Trading License (industrial mineral wholesale) with Hazardous Goods Storage Annex and GOEIC Import/Export Registration Certificate for granular elemental sulfur.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) — Environmental Licensing Department (Law No. 4 of 1994, as amended by Law No. 9 of 2009)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B (Initial Environmental Review) required for wholesale storage and trading; Classification upgraded to Category C (Full EIA Report) if covered sulfur storage capacity exceeds 50 metric tonnes or if any crushing/re-packing operation is attached
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Ambient air: SO₂ ≤ 150 µg/m³ (24-hour) , PM10 ≤ 150 µg/m³ (24-hour), dust fall ≤ 10 t/km²/month per Decree 338/1995 and 471/2014. Wastewater (if any): pH 6.0-9.5, BOD₅ ≤ 60 mg/L, COD ≤ 200 mg/L, TSS ≤ 60 mg/L, sulfides ≤ 1.0 mg/L per Ministerial Decree 44/2000. Sulfur storage must include dust suppression, sealed bagging, dry-protection, and secondary containment; no liquid discharge permitted under the EIA permit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Authority clearance under Fire Protection Law No. 12 of 1996: fire safety certification, fire extinguishing system inspection, sulfur dust-resistance electrical classification, structural load inspection for storage racks, emergency evacuation plan, and workplace occupational clearance from the Ministry of Manpower (Industrial Safety Inspectorate) covering PPE, ventilation, and a written sulfur dust exposure-control program.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance; digital portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation of a Limited Liability Company with the Egyptian General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) and completion of commercial registration with the Commercial Registry, a TP must submit the incorporation contract, commercial registration certificate, lease or title deed, and certified IDs to the local ETA office to obtain the TIN and tax card. VAT registration is effected electronically through the ETA e-tax portal and requires a separate VAT ID. Documents should be authenticated and legally translated if in a foreign language.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or partnership pass-through election is available. The LLC is taxed as a separate juridical entity. Egypt operates a unified corporate tax regime under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005, with no de-merger or hybrid entity election. Specific tax treatment may arise under a tax treaty but no unilateral entity classification election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax) under Law No. 67 of 2016 and its Executive Regulations
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover, per Article 17 of VAT Law 67/2016; mandatory registration for resident and non-resident persons carrying out taxable supplies through an Egyptian fixed establishment. Persons with turnover below the threshold may register voluntarily for refund purposes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt has a mandatory e-invoicing and e-receipt regime operated by the ETA's Electronic Invoicing System. Taxpayers registered on or after January 2021 must integrate their ERP/billing systems with the ETA's REST API and upload invoices in real time. Each invoice receives a unique QR code and UUID; the ETA performs fiscal validation before integration. Failure to report invoices electronically may render them non-deductible and subject to penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods outside Egypt qualify for VAT zero-rating, including regardless of payment of foreign currency proceeds, provided the exporter maintains documentary evidence proving the goods left Egypt. Services supplied to non-residents for direct use outside Egypt, transport services, and services related to exported goods may also be zero-rated. The export must comply with the ETA's rules on 'unjustified forfeiture of tax refunds' and the taxpayer must retain originals or electronic certified files.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (ECS form approved by Customs Authority)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / CMR
Inward Remittance Certificate evidencing receipt of foreign currency at a licensed Egyptian bank
ETA zero-rating worksheet and sworn declaration that goods were exported and delivered outside Egypt
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under VAT Law 67/2016 and Article 28 of the Executive Regulations, a taxpayer claiming unjustified zero-rating or failing to provide the required export documentation shall be subject to VAT at 14% plus statutory delay fines and penalties equal to EGP 500 to EGP 5,000 per invoice for electronic invoicing non-compliance. In case of fraudulent zero-rating evidenced by forged documents, penalties include imprisonment under the Tax Evasion Law No. 202 of 2020 and a fine not exceeding 200% of the tax evaded. The ETA may retroactively claw back VAT refunds and apply the general 15% annual delay interest for a period of up to 5 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), the sole monetary and banking supervisory authority operating under Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Bank and Banking System Law) and its executive regulations, together with CBE foreign-exchange circulars governing authorized-dealer banks, balance-of-payments reporting, and trade-related FX operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Since 6 March 2024, Egypt has operated a flexible, market-determined exchange rate regime; the EGP is freely convertible for current-account transactions (import/export trade flows, freight, insurance, and related services) provided the underlying commercial documentation is presented to an authorized bank. Capital-account inflows (equity subscriptions and shareholder loans) are permitted after submission of notarized corporate resolutions, Commercial Registry updates, and tax registration confirmation; outbound profit and dividend remittances require audited financial statements, evidence that distributable profits arise from Egyptian operations, and a tax clearance certificate from the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA). Sulfur mineral-ore trading under ISIC 4669/HS 2503 is treated as a standard commodity transaction rather than a dual-use or controlled goods category, reducing documentary friction; however, all FX transactions must pass through CBE-licensed banks and be classified under CBE balance-of-payments purpose codes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters of non-oil goods are required under CBE instructions to bring 100% of export proceeds into Egypt through an authorized bank within the CBE-mandated repatriation window, customarily four to five months from the bill-of-lading date. Following the March 2024 FX liberalization, the mandatory conversion of export receipts into EGP was abolished; proceeds may be held in foreign-currency accounts with the collecting bank, and the statutory 'surrender' obligation is limited to repatriation into Egypt via banking channels rather than conversion into EGP. Failure to repatriate within the prescribed period triggers CBE administrative penalties, suspension of trade-finance limits, and heightened ETA audit scrutiny.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational EGP and USD Treasury Account
Operational Account / Export Proceeds Collection Account
Operational Account / Trade-Finance and Import-Export LC Account
Multi-Currency Operational Account with Global Connectivity
Operational Account / LC Settlement and Guarantee Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: LOW as the primary treasury venue; permissible only as an AUXILIARY payment channel. Egypt's regulatory perimeter under Law No. 194 of 2020 confines corporate account-taking, FX clearing, and documentary credit issuance to CBE-licensed banks; offshore EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Corpay) hold no Egyptian banking license and therefore cannot open EGP accounts, execute domestic EGP payments, collect Egyptian export proceeds, or issue letters of credit. Such EMIs may support ancillary foreign-currency payouts (freight, marine insurance, surveyor fees), but they are not authorized dealers for CBE statistical reporting and cannot discharge ETA invoicing obligations, customs-duty settlements, or LC undertakings.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory physical appearance of the LLC's legal representative and each authorized signatory at an Egyptian branch for identity verification and signature specimen capture; fully remote or digital-only account opening is not accepted by CBE-licensed banks for newly formed corporates. Non-resident owners or directors must either travel to Egypt for the onboarding interview or execute a power of attorney before an Egyptian consulate followed by in-branch co-signing; the on-site KYC interview is non-waivable as a practical compliance requirement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Ownership (UBO) opacity where shareholding crosses the statutory 25% threshold without natural-person disclosure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate ownership chart tracing to natural persons, certified passport copies of all UBOs, Commercial Registry extract issued within 3 months, notarized Articles of Association (AOA), board resolution appointing the legal representative, and signed UBO declaration under Egypt's AML Law No. 80 of 2002 and its 2024 amendments

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commercial Registry and tax document inconsistency (expired extract, mismatched ISIC code, or missing VAT registration)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated Commercial Registry certificate (not older than 3 months) reflecting ISIC 4669/HS 2503 activities, unified tax card, VAT registration certificate under Law No. 67 of 2016, ETA clearance attestation, and social insurance registration certificate

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Goods-classification red-flag review for granular elemental sulfur (UN 1350 Class 4.1) as a potential chemical-precursor substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS) proving commodity-grade sulfur, final end-user certificate for agricultural/industrial application, sale and purchase agreements naming the exact product grades, supplier invoices, shipping sample bills of lading, and certificate of origin

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth inquiry on the non-resident shareholder injecting the initial capital into the Egyptian LLC
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: External (non-Egyptian) audited financial statements of the investing shareholder, prior operating bank statements, evidence of lawful business profits supporting the funds, and a signed source-of-funds certification letter addressed to the compliance officer

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, and adverse-media screening hits on counterparties or beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent screening reports (World-Check, Refinitiv, or equivalent), PEP declaration forms, vessel ownership and voyage clearance records confirming no OFAC/EU-sanctioned shipping, and counterparty compliance questionnaires for the sulfur supply chain

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route via SWIFT MT103 from the investing shareholder's bank to the receiving Egyptian bank (National Bank of Egypt SWIFT: NBEGEGCX; CIB SWIFT: CIBEEGCX). Field 70 (Remittance Information) must state a CBE-compliant balance-of-payments purpose descriptor, namely 'Direct Investment / Equity Capital Contribution', and the receiving bank must obtain before crediting: (i) the notarized capital-increase resolution of the LLC, (ii) the updated Commercial Registry certificate reflecting the increased share capital, (iii) the bank deposit certificate issued in accordance with Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, (iv) UBO and AML declarations, and (v) the unified tax card. Upon verification, the receiving bank books the inflow, files the CBE statistical reporting form, and credits either the EGP capital account or a USD-denominated operational account per the entity's treasury instructions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for sulfur purchases use (i) SWIFT MT103 for open-account or sight payments, with Field 50K (ordering customer) and Field 59 (beneficiary bank/account) completed and Field 70 populated with the import purpose descriptor 'Payment for Imports - Goods', supported by proforma invoice, customs declaration evidence, and tax documentation; and (ii) SWIFT MT700 for issuance and MT707 for amendment of irrevocable documentary letters of credit covering bulk sulfur cargoes, typically 90-180 days usance and confirmed by a top-tier international bank where the beneficiary requires sovereign or country-risk mitigation. Export proceeds are collected via inward MT103 into the export proceeds account, with export LC discounting or bills-purchase facilities executed by NBE or CIB trade desks against presentation of the full shipping set (invoice, bill of lading, certificate of origin, insurance certificate, and inspection certificates).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable onshore USD/EGP FX forwards for genuine contracted trade flows, tenors up to 12 months, executed with CBE-licensed authorized banks against confirmed invoices
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on EGP transacted with non-resident counterparty banks to hedge balance-sheet translation risk, noting that NDFs are not permitted onshore
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EGP) tied to underlying trade-finance or working-capital facilities, requiring explicit prior CBE authorization
Natural hedge via matched documentation: denominating both purchase and sale contracts in USD with LC-to-LC back-to-back tenor matching, eliminating open EGP conversion exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Central Department of Corporate Income Tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the close of the annual fiscal year; for a 31 December year-end, by 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 2% per month on the unpaid tax, with a minimum of EGP 500; monthly late-payment interest accrues; enforced collection through bank attachment and seizure is triggered after formal assessment; prolonged non-filing can lead to administrative enforcement and loss of the LLC's clean standing certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual List of Members and Directors (Companies Law Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration Directorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year LLC, by 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The LLC is marked non-compliant in the GAFI register; administrative fines of up to EGP 10,000 may be imposed; amendment and licensing transactions are blocked; two consecutive years of non-filing may trigger strike-off or judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI / Commercial Registry under the beneficial-ownership reporting regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any transfer of quotas or change of beneficial ownership; annual confirmation is included in the Companies Law Annual Return due within 6 months after fiscal year end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-reporting, false declarations or late UBO updates are subject to fines under the AML Law and commercial registry suspension; the registry may restrict shareholder voting rights and freeze the LLC from corporate actions until corrected.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry Renewal and Existence Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Commercial Registry Office under the Ministry of Trade and Industry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the commercial registration anniversary; renewal must be completed before the end of the anniversary month.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs monthly official fines; failure to renew for one year leads to registry deregistration and loss of commercial legal identity, followed by a strike-off procedure.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for all Egyptian LLCs regardless of size; the company must appoint at least one licensed Egyptian auditor, and the auditor's report must accompany the annual corporate income tax return. Regulated entities require a certified audit firm meeting Central Bank of Egypt or Financial Regulatory Authority requirements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), aligned with IFRS; IFRS 9, 15 and 16 apply to banks and FRA-regulated entities; other LLCs prepare statements under EAS with full accrual accounting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each LLC must maintain a beneficial-ownership register at the registered office and update it within 30 days of any transfer of quotas or change in beneficial ownership. The annual Companies Law Return filed with GAFI constitutes the annual confirmation of the UBO register; if no change has occurred, the LLC makes a no-change declaration in the return. Shareholder meetings must resolve and minute any register-related movement with adequate supporting transfer documentation.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,800 – USD 4,500 per year for a small to mid-size LLC in dry-bulk mineral ore trading with letter-of-credit settlement flows

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday for standard LLCs. Preferential 0% corporate income tax may apply within SCZONE licensed projects subject to qualifying conditions. Export-related profits may be exempt under specific conditions. Standard incentives: initial allowance and accelerated depreciation per Law No. 91 of 2005.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Tax Return Form No. 16 for corporate taxpayers; filed electronically via the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) online portal or submitted in person to the competent tax office.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months following the close of the fiscal year. Tax year is generally the calendar year unless otherwise approved. For a December 31 year-end, filing deadline is April 30.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, address, tax card number, commercial registration number, fiscal period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter registration number for EGYPTIAN permanent establishment or branch and foreign parent TIN if registered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State accounting standard applied and currency used (Egyptian Pound unless exemption).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-currency transactions must be converted at Central Bank of Egypt exchange rates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All taxable revenues including trading, brokerage commissions, marine freight income, and ancillary fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Egyptian-source income. Commissions from import/export brokerage involving Egyptian counterparties may be considered Egyptian-source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Purchases of sulfur ore, handling, shipping, marine freight, and direct trading expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support all cross-border payments with contracts, invoices, bills of lading, and bank records to substantiate arm's-length costs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Administrative, employment, rent, professional fees, depreciation, and other allowable deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign head-office allocations must be supported by cost allocation methodology and limited to expenses benefiting the Egyptian PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fines, penalties, bribes, donations not permitted by law, and non-business expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-deductible expenses include foreign taxes paid on behalf of the non-resident parent unless grossed up and deductible under Article 30.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Utilization of losses from prior years, limited to 5 consecutive years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses must be incurred by the Egyptian PE only; foreign losses cannot be deducted. Continuity of activity requirement applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after deductions, exemptions, and loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Taxable income of the PE is the profit attributed to Egyptian activities under the arm's-length principle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax at 22.5% over EGP 200,000; progressive 5% on first EGP 100,000 and 18.75% on next EGP 100,000 for SMEs. Most trading LLCs pay 22.5% on all taxable income above EGP 200,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply treaty provisions if permanent establishment exists. In absence of a PE, file a limited return for other Egyptian-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance income tax paid quarterly, foreign tax credits, and tax withheld at source.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach documentation for foreign tax credits under applicable tax treaty; only direct taxes attributable to Egyptian-source income may be creditable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final liability after withholding and quarterly advance tax instalments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: None. Ensure quarterly advance tax payments (1% of gross revenue for trading activities) were made on time to avoid delay penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of the tax due per month or part-month, capped at 100% of tax due. Late payment penalty: 5% of unpaid tax per month, capped at 100%. Failure to file return may result in additional 10% penalty. Negligence or evasion penalties up to 100% of tax understatement; interest at 3% above Central Bank discount rate may apply. Criminal fines for intentional evasion may amount to EGP 20,000 to EGP 2,000,000 or imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on gross dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders under Law 91/2005. Egyptian corporate shareholders are exempt under participation exemption.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced DTA rate, beneficial owner must obtain Tax Residency Certificate from home country, submit to ETA with treaty relief claim form, provide beneficial ownership declaration, and comply with minimum holding period (generally 12 months). ETA issues approval; withholding at treaty rate may be applied in advance or reclaimed through refund procedures. Required documentation includes TRC, audited financial statements, and agreement documents.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and technical services: statutory rate 20% on gross amount, reduced under treaties to 5%–15%. Interest: statutory rate 10% on payments to non-residents; reduced treaty rate generally 5%–10%. Management fees are treated as service fees taxable at 20% unless characterized as business profits under a DTA.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 4,000,000 annual related-party transaction threshold for mandatory Local File and Master File. Penalties for noncompliance up to EGP 1,000,000. Related-party transactions must be disclosed in Annual TP Declaration Form.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt has no formal ESR framework but requires genuine substance and actual commercial activity. Arrangements lacking commercial substance may be disregarded under General Anti-Abuse Rules and Article 32 of Law 91/2005. The ETA may adjust profits based on functions performed, assets used, and risks assumed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting revenues, inflating deductions, false documentation, concealed foreign bank accounts, fabricated purchase contracts, or misreporting expenses for sulfur trading and brokerage.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment for tax evasion (up to 5 years) and fine of EGP 10,000 to EGP 500,000; additional administrative fine up to 100% of tax understatement. Criminal proceedings under Law 91/2005.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who intentionally participate in tax evasion before personally liable for fines and penalties; may face imprisonment, travel bans, property seizure, and civil liability for unpaid corporate taxes under tax law veil-piercing provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Late filing or non-filing of annual tax return, failure to withhold WHT on dividends, royalties, interest, failure to pay quarterly advance tax, failure to file TP declaration, or failure to submit books and records on audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late filing fines (5% per month up to 100% tax), late payment fines (5% per month up to 100% tax), fixed penalties up to EGP 50,000 for failure to submit required forms, and revocation of tax registration licenses in repeated cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for penalties if they knowingly cause noncompliance. In extreme cases, criminal fines against responsible managers under ETA enforcement; no imprisonment for purely civil late filing unless fraud is present.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's-length pricing of sulfur ore purchase or resale, excessive brokerage or freight fees to related foreign entities, lack of TP documentation, or failure to use approved method with proper benchmarking study.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income; penalty equal to 25% of the TP adjustment amount (per ETA TP Guidelines); late payment fines and interest; failure to submit TP documentation may result in additional 10% penalty. Potential aggregate fine up to 100% of adjusted tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors responsible for implementing related-party arrangements may be personally liable for additional tax if they acted beyond authority or misrepresented facts. Criminal liability only when TP manipulation is part of a tax evasion scheme.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: LLC is established as a shell without actual office, staff, or activity while profits are claimed to be earned outside Egypt; transactions booked through Egypt to access treaty benefits or lower effective taxation; no physical substance for trading activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR may deny benefits; ETA may ignore the shell entity and assess tax against foreign principal; sanctions include revocation of tax registration, fines, and denial of treaty relief. Under Egyptian law, shell companies misusing commercial register may face administrative penalties and deregistration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be subject to travel bans and personal liability for taxes if they act as nominee directors for sham entities. Involvement in circular transactions or fraudulent invoices could give rise to criminal liability for facilitating tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Trade Finance Red Flags
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using letters of credit to disguise payments for sanctionable goods, illicit cash payments for sulfur cargo, tampering with shipping documents, breaching bank AML/KYC, or facilitating sanctions-evasion through third-country transshipment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violations under Egyptian AML Law No. 80 of 2002: imprisonment up to 15 years and fines from EGP 200,000 to EGP 10,000,000. Corporate fines may reach EGP 5,000,000; freezing of accounts, assets, and cargo; revocation of license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be personally and criminally liable for AML violations. Civil liability for damages; travel bans and asset freezes; in serious cases, imprisonment and extradition. Negligent failure to obtain necessary licenses is also culpable.
